topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kryvyi Rih, President Zelenskyy's hometown, killed 2 people (4 sources). The strikes follow Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks on the Kerch Bridge, which Zelensky called a "fair response" to 109 Russian aerial attacks on Ukrainian bridges. Separately, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland (7 sources); the Polish prime minister called it a likely provocation timed to European military drills. Other items include Denmark's accusation of a Russian assassination plot and expulsion of a Russian defense attache, a reported drone strike on a Kaliningrad-bound ship in the Gulf of Finland, and US-Russia talk of postwar European security arrangements.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians in a World Central Kitchen vehicle in Gaza City, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and witnesses (3 sources). Saudi Arabia says it intercepted three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh, and two tanker incidents were reported near Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran blamed a naval mine for one fire. Two sources report the US and Israel are considering a new assault on Iran, though it is unclear whether Trump is willing. A single outlet reports an IRGC claim of damaging a US F-16, which CENTCOM denies. Iran's foreign minister also said Iran is having a 'major strategic debate' on its nuclear doctrine.
topics.T15: Florida is dealing with historic flooding, and evacuation alerts have been issued along the St. Johns River (2 sources). A magnitude 6.7 earthquake in Peru reportedly damaged homes and caused rockfalls that disrupted roads in Junín and Lima. Other items are minor or preparedness-related: the Macquarie Island seismic station outage shortening tsunami response time for Australia, Cyclone Akvan evacuations in Ganjam, India, and El Niño-related king tide and insurance stories in California.
topics.T01: The items are scattered and mostly single-sourced. Myanmar's military reportedly carried out airstrikes, including one in Paletwa township that killed at least eight civilians including an infant. A Houthi-aligned outlet reports Saudi air and artillery attacks on Yemeni governorates. A US congressional commission warned that China's military support for Pakistan raises the risk of a two-front conflict for India (2 sources), and Rep. Tlaib reacted to renewed Trump threats to invade Cuba. The rest is commentary or speeches.
topics.T02: Coverage is mostly feature and advocacy reporting rather than a single event. The most widely carried item (3 sources) is Rohingya Australians welcoming the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide. Other stories cover displaced elderly people and disabled children in Sudan, a Greater Horn of Africa food insecurity response plan, Haiti's farmers facing violence, hunger and El Niño, and displaced people and out-of-school children in Nigeria's northwest.
topics.T03: Iran denied US allegations of chemical and biological weapons development, accusing Washington of repeating the pre-Iraq-war intelligence failures (2 sources). A separate analysis piece discusses bioterrorism risk and the Aum Shinrikyo precedent. No attack was reported.
topics.T04: Malawi tightened border screening and imposed quarantine rules to prevent Ebola importation from the DRC (2 sources). Germany reportedly updated its Uganda travel alert, citing transit restrictions and possible 21-day quarantine for travelers who have visited the DRC. Also reported were a bird flu quarantine across two counties with a cull of nearly 1.8M chickens, and a research paper on H3N2 influenza in dogs in Alabama.
topics.T05: Coverage is sparse: a single outlet reports that imprisoned former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro was hospitalized with intense abdominal pain, and that his son alleges 'psychological torture'. No wider instability or coup indicators appear in today's items.
topics.T06: An analysis piece carried by 9 sources claims 114 communist, Marxist and socialist groups powered an 'International Youth Strike' across 24 countries; its framing is opinion-based and not independently verified. In France, riots broke out for a sixth consecutive weekend with 82,500 demonstrators counted nationwide by the Interior Ministry, a declining turnout (4 sources). Italy saw a nationwide strike over wages and living costs, and a partisan US piece alleges foreign-linked activist networks are driving protests.
topics.T07: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said the case for changing Iran's nuclear doctrine has 'strong logic' because NPT membership did not prevent its nuclear facilities from being bombed. Trump said the US would find out whether Iran is attempting to build a dirty bomb and 'will not allow that', referring to a rumour. Trump also commented on possible US-Russia-China nuclear talks. All three items are single-source.
topics.T08: Nigeria's military says air strikes killed 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno and that 26 fighters and family members surrendered in the North-East (2 sources). Other items are single-source: a militant killed after an attack on a police van in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, five Christians reportedly killed by herdsmen in Plateau State, and a UK conviction of a white supremacist for plotting to burn down an asylum hotel. Haiti also announced a deal with El Salvador to build prisons.
topics.T09: An American detained in Cuba for nearly a decade was released (4 sources). The available summary gives no further detail.
topics.T10: Items are mostly single-source and unrelated. They include Pakistan's intensified missile testing, projected cost growth of about $275 billion tied to Trump-class battleships, and a Denmark security agreement giving the US greater military access in Greenland. Others cover the US and Russia blocking rules on autonomous weapons, US-Canada intelligence modernization, and a Kosovo mortar test.
topics.T11: Pakistan-Indonesia counter-terrorism exercise Elang Strike-III concluded (5 sources), India and Malaysia began the Harimau Shakti drill, and the Nigerian Army began a two-week exercise in Oyo (2 sources). Also noted is that the Russian missiles that landed in Poland coincided with European exercises there, which is covered under Russia / Ukraine.
topics.T12: Hackers reportedly breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center database, CNN reported, the second FBI targeting in months (4 sources). This comes amid a roughly 10-day wave of US outages affecting JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft and air travel, which officials say were not intentional attacks. President Trump replaced the top cybersecurity official, and lawmakers and experts are questioning the early dismissal of cyberattack as a cause. A MoEngage vendor-credential breach and a Europe cyber-weakness analysis were also reported.
topics.T13: Coverage is sparse and largely opinion or retrospective. Spanish police reportedly believe 10,000 identical inflatables were distributed ahead of a July incursion into Ceuta, and one outlet reports roughly 11,000 West Africans arrived on a Canary island on 100 boats. Other items are political commentary on migration.
topics.T16: Trump floated chief of staff Stephen Miller as a 2028 presidential candidate (2 sources). Spain's main party leaders clashed in an election debate, with polls pointing to a possible conservative government backed by the far right (2 sources). Nigeria's 2027 campaign is also in view, and several single-source partisan pieces make unverified claims that the 2026 US midterms were rigged.
